title: P5-45 Preserve event drafts and fix member email and Help navigation
body:
## Associated User Story

[P5-45: Fix bugs](https://pt-502.atlassian.net/browse/P5-45)

As an officer or member, I want event drafts to survive location-map problems, long email addresses to fit the home page, and public Help pages to provide a clear path back to login.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Event form values are preserved when the map loads or a location is chosen.

- Sunny: An officer fills in the event name, description, start time, and end time, then loads the map or chooses a location. All entered values remain, the location coordinates update, and the event saves with those values.
- Rainy: The map provider is blocked or fails to load, or geolocation permission is denied. The form retains the draft, explains the problem, and allows manual coordinates or a named location with both coordinates left blank. Partial or out-of-range coordinates are rejected. An event without a map pin cannot use location-based QR check-in until a pin is added.

### Long email addresses fit the member home page without overlapping nearby content.

- Sunny: A member with an email address longer than 50 characters opens the home page. The full address wraps within its statistic card, and badges, other statistics, and buttons remain readable.
- Rainy: The address has no natural word breaks or the viewport is narrow. The address still stays inside the card, and the page does not gain horizontal scrolling.

### Signed-out Help pages provide a visible Back to login link.

- Sunny: A signed-out visitor follows Help from the login page and uses the top Back to login link to return.
- Rainy: A signed-out visitor opens Help directly from a bookmark or on a phone. The link is still present and works without relying on browser history or a referrer.

## Definition of Done

A story is done when its acceptance criteria are met and every item in the team PR template is satisfied:

(A) code review by a non-author, coding standard met, RuboCop checked with output/CI link, and setup changes documented;

(B) the human-only maintainability checks (meaningful comments and names, skinny controllers, thin views, DRY, Rails conventions, foreign keys, enums, nested routes);

(C) tests added or updated and passing. Any deferred items or RuboCop exclusions are explained in Section D of the PR.

## Evidence

### Tests pass

Local validation of this branch:

```text

555 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending

node --test spec/javascript/*.cjs
13 tests passed, 0 failed
```

Added JavaScript regression tests for delayed/blocked maps, reconnects during loading, manual coordinate validation, and denied geolocation. Updated Rails coverage for saving without a pin, preserving form values after validation errors, and direct public Help-to-login navigation.

### Rubocop

```text

161 files inspected, no offenses detected
```

[GitHub Actions for this branch](https://github.com/FA26-CSCE431-software-engineering/PT-502/actions?query=branch%3Ap5-45-ui-bug-fixes)

### Manual checks and documentation

Verified normal and blocked map loading with a filled draft, saved-location selection, and saving the event. Checked long-email containment at 1280, 375, and 320 pixels with no horizontal page overflow. Checked login-to-Help-to-login navigation and direct mobile Help access.

Updated the officer/member Help instructions and the event-form, event-check-in, and member-home screenshots.

CI now installs Node.js 22 and runs all JavaScript regression tests; the README documents the command. No new application dependency or database migration is required.

### Conflict resolution and integration validation

Merged the updated `main` (through `420f769`) into this branch and combined the stylesheet and officer-guide changes. Preserved the existing event-import instructions, the map fallback guidance, and all original P5-45 commits and timestamps.

The member-table template matches the corrected version now on `main`, preserving filtering, sortable headings, member import, the admins table, and manager-only actions.

title: Time tweak
body:
# Associated User Story

As an officer/manager creating an event, I should not be able to set the end time before the start time at all, as all end time possible times should be starting after the start time.

# Acceptance Criteria

### Officers and managers cannot set an event’s end time before its start time, and only valid end times can be chosen.

**Sunny:** An officer or manager creates or edits an event and picks a start date and time. The end time options then only include times after the start time, so an earlier end time cannot be selected. They choose a valid end time and save, and the event is created with the start and end times shown on the event details page. If they later move the start time to after the current end time, the end time is cleared or adjusted and they are asked to pick a new valid one before saving.

**Rainy:** The officer or manager tries to get around the restriction, for example by typing an end time earlier than or equal to the start time, or by submitting the form manually with an invalid end time. They see a clear message next to the field, such as “End time must be after the start time,” instead of a blank page or a silent failure. The event is not saved until the end time is fixed, and any previously saved times stay unchanged. A regular member who tries to create or edit an event is blocked (officers and managers only).

# Definition of Done

title: Import Attendance like events
body:
# Associated User Story

As an officer, I want to upload attendance for an event the same way I upload events, so that I can record who showed up in one step and members’ points and active status stay accurate without me entering each person by hand.

# Acceptance Criteria

**Officers can upload an attendance file and see each member credited for the event they attended.**

- Sunny: An officer opens the attendance upload, picks a file (e.g., CSV) listing the event and the members who attended, and confirms. The system matches each row to an existing event and member, saves the attendance, and shows a success message with how many records were recorded. Those members’ total points, points by event type (service vs. personal development), and active status (7+ points) update to reflect the new attendance.

- Rainy: The file is the wrong format, is missing required columns, or has rows that can’t be matched (unknown event, unknown member, or a duplicate entry). The officer sees a clear message with the row number and reason for each problem instead of a blank page or a silent failure. Valid rows can still be imported, nothing is counted twice, and a regular member who tries to access the upload is blocked (officers only).

title: Departing members
body:
# Associated User Story

As a manager, I want a way for a member to manually leave the organization and disappear from the member sheet, and to manually be able to remove them. So that I can manage which individuals are in my organization.

# Acceptance Criteria

### Members can leave the organization, and officers can remove them, so they disappear from the member sheet

**Sunny:** A member clicks "Leave Organization" and confirms, or an officer selects a member and clicks "Remove Member" and confirms. The person disappears from the member sheet and dashboard, and they can no longer access member features. The other members' data is not affected.

**Rainy:** The removal fails, the person is removed by accident, or a regular member tries to remove someone else. If it fails, the officer or member sees an error and the person stays on the sheet, rather than ending up half-removed. A confirmation prompt appears before anything is removed. body:
Bumps [omniauth](https://github.com/omniauth/omniauth) from 2.1.4 to 2.3.1.
Changelog

Sourced from omniauth's changelog.

[2.3.1] - 2026-10-22

Fixed

  • remember_sign_in no longer raises KeyError when called outside the request phase, before omniauth.params is stored, as when a provider gem's specs call authorize_params directly.

[2.3.0] - 2026-10-22

Added

  • Let strategies keep the origin and params of several sign-ins in progress at once, for example in several tabs, so each callback gets its own instead of the latest sign-in's. A strategy opts in by calling remember_sign_in in its request phase with a value the provider sends back, such as OAuth 2.0's state, and overriding callback_sign_in_key. The latest 5 are stored in session['omniauth.sign_ins'], and omniauth.origin and omniauth.params still hold the latest one. See the README. (omniauth-oauth2#195)

Changed

  • The gem no longer includes CHANGELOG.md, which was about half its size. Its changelog_uri links to the changelog on GitHub.

[2.2.0] - 2026-10-22

Added

  • Add a full_host option for each strategy, as a string or a proc that takes the Rack env. It takes precedence over OmniAuth.config.full_host. (#835)
  • Ship RBS type signatures for OmniAuth in sig/.
  • Document the Rack env keys OmniAuth sets, CSRF protection, sending origin as a form field, and how SameSite session cookies affect the callback in the README. (#909, #1075, #1048, #1149)
  • Add this changelog.

Changed

  • omniauth.params now includes params posted to the request phase's form, not just its query string, so they survive the POST-only request phase introduced in 2.0. The authenticity_token param is never included (see CVE-2017-18076 under 1.3.2). If your request form posts other fields, they now appear in omniauth.params and are stored in the session until the callback. (#975)
  • OmniAuth::Builder builds its middleware stack on the first request and reuses it, instead of rebuilding every strategy on every request. Providers added after the first request are ignored. (#1083, #970)
  • Strategy#call sends a request that isn't on the strategy's request or callback path straight to the app, instead of duplicating the strategy for it. It still duplicates it in test mode, with an other_phase, with path lambdas, or when the strategy overrides how #call! dispatches. Methods patched directly onto OmniAuth::Strategy, rather than overridden in a subclass, aren't detected, so a patched #call! no longer runs for requests outside the strategy's paths. (#1172)

title: Event location proximity in feet
body:
# Associated User Story

As an officer/manager creating an event, I want the location proximity to be something like 250 feet (not in meters), and able to adjust. 

# Acceptance Criteria

**Officers and managers can set an event’s location proximity in feet, and adjust it as needed**

- Sunny: An officer or manager creates or edits an event and sees a “Location proximity” field labeled in feet, pre-filled with a default of 250 feet. They can change it to any value within the allowed range (e.g., 100 to 1,000 feet) and save. The system stores the value, shows it in feet on the event details page, and uses it when checking whether a member is close enough to the event location. Changing the value later updates the check for that event without affecting other events.

- Rainy: The officer or manager enters a value that is blank, non-numeric, zero or negative, or outside the allowed range. They see a clear message next to the field explaining the problem (e.g., “Enter a proximity between 100 and 1,000 feet”) instead of a blank page or a silent failure. The event is not saved until the value is fixed, and any previously saved proximity stays unchanged. A regular member who tries to create or edit an event, or change its proximity, is blocked (officers and managers only).

# Associated User Story
As a user, I want to be able to submit an event that is not a PT event to an officer for approval, but can count towards my points.

As an officer, I want a window where I can see forms for members submitting proposals for outside special events to count towards their point total.

### Members can submit a non-PT event for officer review, and once an officer approves it, the points are added to the member's total and the correct point type.
- Sunny: A member fills out a submission form with the event name, date, point type (e.g., service, personal development, social), and a short description or proof of attendance, then submits it. The member sees a confirmation and the request shows as "pending" in their dashboard. Officers see the request in an approval queue with all the submitted details. When an officer approves it, the points are added to the member's dashboard under the correct point type, their active status updates if they now meet the minimums, and the member sees the status change to "approved." Only officers can access the approval queue and approve or deny requests.

# Associated User Story
As a manager, I want to have different types of points for attendance, and have a certain number of each point type determine member status rather than total points.

As an officer, I don’t have to be tracked in the point dashboard because there is no point requirement for me.

# Acceptance Criteria
### Manager can define point types and set a minimum required for each type, and member status is based on meeting those minimums instead of total points.
- Sunny: A manager opens the point settings and sees the available point types (e.g., service, personal development, social). They set a minimum for each type (e.g., 3 service, 2 personal development, 2 social) and save. When a member attends an event, the points are added to the correct type. A member who meets every minimum shows as "active." A member who has enough total points but is below the minimum in any single type shows as "inactive," with the missing requirement noted (e.g., "needs 1 more service point").
-Rainy: A manager tries to save a point requirement that is invalid (a blank field, a negative number, or a non-number), the settings fail to save, or a regular member tries to change the requirements. The system shows a clear error message (e.g., "Enter a whole number of 0 or more" or "Changes could not be saved, try again or contact an admin") instead of failing silently or saving bad values. The previous requirements stay in place so member statuses aren't accidentally changed, and only officers can edit the settings.
###Officers are excluded from point tracking and active/inactive status, and they do not appear as members who need to meet point requirements.
-Sunny: A member is promoted to officer. Their name no longer appears in the point dashboard, and they are not counted toward any active or inactive totals. They are never shown as "inactive" or flagged for missing points, even if they have no points or are below the minimums. Officers can still view the dashboard to see regular members' points and statuses. If an officer is later changed back to a regular member, they reappear in the dashboard and are tracked from that point on, with any points they had already earned still counted.
- Rainy: The system can't tell whether someone is an officer (for example, the role fails to load or the role data is missing), or an officer's role is changed and the dashboard doesn't update. The system shows a clear message (e.g., "We couldn't confirm this member's role, try again or contact an admin") instead of wrongly marking an officer as inactive or hiding a regular member from tracking. When the role status is uncertain, the member's existing status stays unchanged until the role can be confirmed, so no one is incorrectly flagged or dropped from the dashboard.

Sourced from simplecov's releases.

Bugfixes

v1.3.1

Bugfixes

  • cover_views compiles templates on Rails main again. Rails removed ActionView::Template.registered_template_handler; the lookup reads ActionView::Template::Handlers.template_handlers and still skips an extension with no handler. See simplecov-ruby/simplecov#1300.
  • require "simplecov" works again on JRuby on Windows, where 1.3.0 raised LoadError: Could not open library '.../libprism.dll'. Prism's FFI backend cannot open its native library there, and 1.3.0 required Prism as soon as SimpleCov loaded. Prism now loads only when branch or method coverage needs the static extractor, which a line-only run never does. Where it cannot load at all, the extractor falls back to empty branch and method tables for never-loaded files, as it did before 1.3.0. See simplecov-ruby/simplecov#1299.
  • simplecov affected --run works on JRuby on Windows, where it crashed with NoMethodError because Process.wait2 answers no status there. On that platform the runner starts through Kernel#system instead.
  • simplecov serve refuses a symlink that points outside the report on JRuby on Windows too. JRuby's File.realpath follows no symlinks there, so serve would have served the file the link pointed to, and simplecov clean and the coverage.json lookup compared paths that were never resolved. On JRuby the CLI now resolves paths through the JDK.

v1.3.0

SimpleCov 1.3 raises the minimum Ruby to 3.3, brings the coverage directives to ERB, Haml, and Slim templates, teaches simplecov patch and simplecov uncovered to annotate CI hosts natively, and settles what the report says about files and groups that hold nothing.

v1.7.0 [2026-10-02] Lars Kanis lars@greiz-reinsdorf.de

  • Remove enforced rpath addition when no rpath is configured in rbconfig. #699

title: Manager role elevation: promote/demote members
body:
Associated User Story
As a club manager, I want to be able to log into the app with the
highest roles, so I can do all the same functions as officers, as
well as promote and demote members to and from officers.


Manager can log in and access manager-only tools that regular members can't

Sunny: An officer or club manager signs in with their TAMU Google account and sees the officer-only features (member tracker, create event, edit points, promote/demote members) in addition to the normal member features.

Rainy: A regular member, or someone with no manager role, signs in or tries to open an officer-only page directly (e.g., by URL).   • Groups that match no files are omitted from the report instead of padding it at 100%, and the rails profile declares its groups alphabetically.
  • cover_views is the only way to measure a template now: a cover glob that matches one warns and leaves it out, and ignore: :eval_generated no longer drops a template's real branches and methods.
  • A file with nothing to cover reports the same percentage in the file list as it does in the source view.

Upgrade notes

  • The minimum supported Ruby is now 3.3. Ruby 3.2 reached end of life in March 2026. JRuby 10 remains supported for line coverage.
  • A group that matched no files disappears from the HTML report, coverage.json, and the history file, and a per-group minimum on it passes silently rather than complaining that the group does not exist.
  • The rails profile's group tabs come out in alphabetical order, so an existing project's tabs move.
  • A never-loaded file with no branches or methods reports 100% for those criteria rather than 0%, so a per-file branch or method threshold that failed such a file passes now. A file the report carries no branch or method table for at all is still unaccounted for, and keeps its 0%.

Prism is bundled with every supported Ruby, so the static coverage extractor stops probing for it: StaticCoverageExtractor.available? and the empty-hash fallbacks for its absence are gone. So is the emulation of Ruby 3.2's constant folding, where parentheses were transparent for every literal and a folded dead arm's branches survived in the branch table.

Enhancements

  • # simplecov:disable and # simplecov:enable work inside ERB, Haml, and Slim templates measured with cover_views, in each language's own comment syntax (<%# simplecov:disable %>, -# simplecov:disable, / simplecov:disable) or as Ruby comments on a code line. The scan now reads only the Ruby a template holds, at the template's own lines, so a Devise app can disable the confirmable link it never renders instead of carrying it as uncovered.   • Groups that match no files are omitted from the report instead of appearing as 100% covered with nothing in them.   • simplecov patch and simplecov uncovered annotate CI hosts natively. --annotate KIND on both commands turns the answer into inline annotations in the host's own channel, one per contiguous missed range with project-relative paths (patch adds one per uncovered touched branch or method when the report measured them): github emits ::warning workflow commands, gitlab a Code Quality report for the codequality artifact, rdjson reviewdog's Diagnostic Format for any host reviewdog posts to, azure ##vso[task.logissue] logging commands, teamcity code inspection service messages, and buildkite the Markdown body for buildkite-agent annotate. uncovered previously offered only github, and its annotations now name the chosen criterion the way patch's do. Nothing else reaches stdout in that mode and patch --minimum still sets the exit status, so one CI step can annotate and gate. Documented under CI annotations in docs/CLI.md.

Bugfixes

  • A file with no branches or no methods reports the same percentage everywhere. A file tracked but never loaded had its empty branch and method sets forced to 0% (simplecov-ruby/simplecov#902), from a time when simulation recorded no tuples for such a file and an empty set really did mean "nobody knows". Simulation has synthesized those tuples statically for a while now, so an empty set is a fact about the file: it has no branches, or a directive skipped the ones it has. Such a file now reports 100% the way a loaded file with none always has, so the file list stops showing 0% beside a source view that says 100%, and a per-file branch or method minimum stops failing a file that has nothing to cover. A file carrying no table at all for the criterion is still unaccounted for, and 0% stands there. The HTML report's source view also takes each header percentage from the report rather than recomputing it from the fraction, so the two views cannot drift again. See simplecov-ruby/simplecov#1296.
  • A cover glob that matches a template warns and leaves it out instead of simulating it. Simulation classifies lines as Ruby and parses for branches, so a swept-in template appeared with a comment counted as a missed line, an #id tag counted as never relevant, and no branches at all. The warning names the templates and points at cover_views, which compiles them and measures the real thing.
  • The deprecated # :nocov: toggle works in a template's own comment syntax (<%# :nocov: %>, -# :nocov:, / :nocov:) and emits its deprecation warning there. The matcher read raw lines and needed the line to begin with #, so those forms were silently ignored while the Ruby-comment form inside an ERB code tag happened to work. The matcher now reads the same extracted Ruby the directives do.
  • ignore: :eval_generated no longer drops a template's real branches and methods. The filter keeps a Coverage entry only when Prism finds a matching construct in the static source, which for a template measured with cover_views meant parsing ERB, Haml, or Slim as Ruby. That usually fails and the entry is kept, but a template whose text happens to parse (a Haml or Slim #id tag reads as a Ruby comment, and so does an ERB text line starting with #) yielded a confident wrong parse, and the template's own conditionals vanished from branch coverage. Templates now skip the parse, since everything a template reports is eval-generated by construction and the filter has nothing to distinguish there.
Commits

  • b2aec76 Drop support for Ruby 3.2
  • 5e869ef Report a file with no branches as fully covered everywhere
  • e425d8b Warn and leave out templates a cover glob matches
  • 12d7914 Honor the deprecated nocov toggle in template comments
  • 7d278ea Exempt templates from the eval_generated filter
  • b39506d Honor simplecov directives inside Haml and Slim templates
  • c5233a4 Honor simplecov directives inside ERB templates
  • 5a8f224 Alphabetize the rails profile's groups by name
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view
